assessments.reasoning: The survey design allows evaluating elements of female-headed and women-maintained households to varying degrees. For de_jure_vs_de_facto: marital status (Col 07) combined with household relationship/presence of partner (Col 03) and remittance/alimony receipts from non-residents (Bloque V ítem 12) allows distinguishing de jure female heads (unpartnered by marital status) from de facto female heads (married/partnered women whose partners are absent from the household roster or who depend on external financial support). For unpartnered_mother_child_units: relationship to head (Col 03) only records relationship relative to the designated head of household ('Jefe/a'), meaning mother-child sub-units within extended or multi-family households cannot be systematically identified when the mother is not the head. For women_maintained_by_provider: individual labor income (Cuestionario Individual) and disaggregated non-labor income by individual member (Cuestionario Hogar Bloque VI) together with sex (Col 04) allow identifying whether a woman is the primary economic provider/income contributor of the household regardless of who is reported as head. For mother_child_unit_activity: consumption and living arrangements are defined strictly at the aggregate household level ('comparten los gastos de alimentación y/o otros gastos esenciales'), with no mechanism to attribute consumption, production, or care activities to a sub-household mother-child hearth-hold unit.
